newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia outlines telecom privatisation plans.
newsitem.headline: Serbia outlines telecom privatisation plans.

text.p: The Serbian PTT plans to offer a 30 percent stake in the company for privatisation after a year-long reform which is due to start in March, the state company's director general Milorad Jaksic said on Tuesday.
He told the telecommunications forum Telfor'96 that telecommunications would be the first strategic sector to be privatised in Serbia.
"The new law on telecommunications is the first step towards reform and separation of the postal and telecommunications units of the PTT," he added.
The law would determine which telecommunication services would be privatised and specify the criteria for choosing operators and their number.
Jaksic said the partial privatisation of the telecommunications sector could begin with the adoption of the law and completion of the restructuring of the PTT expected by March 1998.
Current privatisation law allows Yugoslav companies to sell off stakes of up to 49 percent but the PTT has opted for a two-stage floatation.
"We looked into Hungarian and Czech privatisation models and believe that selling up to 30 percent stake at first would be the best," Jaksic told Reuters.
The remainder would be preserved and sold to workers at a later stage, he added.
"We hope to raise between one and two billion dollars through privatisation and the money will be invested in future development of telecommunications in Serbia," Jaksic said.
The PTT is aiming to establish a strategic alliance with Western telecommunications companies.
Preliminary estimates, prepared by the Belgrade-based private institute for economic research CES-Mecon, valued the Serbian telecommunications unit at around $5 billion.
PTT officials said accountants Pricewater House, Salomon Brothers and Deloitte & Touche had been asked to verify the valuation and a final estimate was expected in January or February 1997.
Jaksic said PTT would chose its future partners through international tender.
Serbia needed around $6 billion by 2005 to launch three million new telephone lines and double the number of lines to 40 per 100 inhabitants.
In 1996, the PTT moved aggressively to improve telecommunications which deteriorated during 3-1/2 years of UN economic sanctions and neglect.
It said it would meet its 1996 plan to install 710,000 new phone lines. So far, 630,000 new lines have been installed.
